Purpose and exclusions

Make failures explainable without turning logging into another mutable gameplay database. Economic ledgers provide durable accounting; operational metrics explain latency, rejection and content balance.

Never bypass the declared rule owner, mutate an authored definition at runtime, trust a client completion claim, or infer a compiled implementation from this page.

Creation and configuration

  1. Author a controlled error catalog in DA_TelemetryPolicy_Default and map codes to localization keys rather than exposing backend stack traces.
  2. Reopen merchant, gathering, fishing and crafting handlers to record the same command/receipt IDs in their result events.
  3. Build WBP_Diagnostics as a development-only screen with read-only epoch/revision/command state; never add buttons that directly set currency on production clients.
  4. Create a synthetic purchase sequence from 1000 to 950 currency, a sell/buyback and a failed full-bag craft. Compare ledger changes to dashboard events.
  5. Document retention/access and a minimal support report format: build, zone, approximate time, command ID, observed and expected behavior.

Required sequence: create native prerequisites -> actual build -> child/data creation -> configure -> assign to listed consumer -> save -> run named fixture. A compiled shell without its consumer assignment is not feature completion.

Functions, commands and event bindings

Project custom contracts are not engine/plugin nodes. A read-only asset participates through its consumer; it does not inherit that consumer’s mutation methods. Backend endpoint pages label transport proposals explicitly.

ContractExecution / effect

QueryOwnCommandStatus(CommandId) -> Pending|Receipt|Unknown; backend authenticated readNative current owner; local request versus server validation as the command states. Backend work is asynchronous, cosmetics observe only after accepted state.
ExportSupportDiagnostics(Consent, RedactionPolicy) -> RedactedBundle|DeclinedNative current owner; local request versus server validation as the command states. Backend work is asynchronous, cosmetics observe only after accepted state.

Lifecycle and cleanup

  1. Construct with only safe defaults; no service calls or world scans from construction scripts.
  2. Inject current owner/definition/session and subscribe once after readiness. Possession and replicated state may arrive in either order; guard initialization.
  3. Accept only permitted commands under current identity/epoch; keep local UI/cosmetic prediction separate from committed state.
  4. After server/backend result apply only matching request generation and nonstale revision; late reply to old body does not mutate new body.
  5. On death, transfer, disconnect, restart or teardown cancel transient work, clear input/timers, unbind delegates and release weak observers. Durable receipts remain authoritative.
  6. On reconnect create fresh runtime objects from current committed snapshot; never deserialize old Actor/widget pointers or rerun initial grants.

Concrete player-to-authority flow

Participation in Diagnostics, economy telemetry and support evidence. Rule owner: URPGTelemetryAdapter. This asset’s role is Make failures explainable without turning logging into another mutable gameplay database. Economic ledgers provide durable accounting; operational metrics explain latency, rejection and content balance.

  1. Attach one correlation ID when an interaction begins and propagate it through the owned RPC and backend command.
  2. Commit the economic receipt and audit delta in the durable transaction; telemetry emission occurs after commit and can retry through the documented outbox without regranting.
  3. UI shows Pending, Accepted or a friendly localized reason; diagnostics show the stable command ID for support.
  4. Dashboards aggregate currency sources/sinks, item generation/destruction, rejection rates, gather yields and merchant stock pressure.
  5. A metric sink outage does not block a valid committed transaction; required audit persistence failure does block a transaction whose policy requires it.
  6. Support exports remove access tokens, private chat and machine secrets and identify build/catalog version before user approval.

Named fixture and acceptance

Fixture: L_Rillmere / purchase-craft-gather receipt fixtures. Configure this asset at its first phase and run the linked phase recipe. Actual result: not run in Unreal/backend during documentation generation.

Stimulus / expected result
Metric sink down -> transaction receipt still durable, UI confirms from authority.
Duplicate receipt delivery -> dashboard de-duplicates by receipt/event ID; no second economic grant.
Unknown error code -> generic safe message plus correlation ID, not a credential-containing exception.
Support bundle review -> tokens and service credentials absent.

Record expected/observed separately. Reopen the concrete map consumer; inspect authoritative state, stable IDs/revisions and UI. Static link checks cannot satisfy this gameplay test.

Common mistakes and staged limits

Do not duplicate a native rule in Blueprint, assume a planned type is compiled, or keep callbacks/owners valid after world or session replacement.

Do not build later references as empty shells in an earlier phase. Source-derived art rows remain blocked by the missing ZIP; plugin API bindings remain blocked by installed-source verification. Placeholder visuals and proposed tuning are explicitly not production proof.
